title: Working in Capitol's editing room
summary: McRae edited tapes at Capitol, including Sinatra material, and mostly wrote rather than played.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring

blocks.x: Well, let's see. Moving on, what other recordings were you involved with for Capitol with Dave Cavanaugh?

Well we did some other things for him, but, you know --
I think we did some of the -- I think a lot of tapes came in.
I was working in the editing room -- we used to edit a lot of stuff. That was a good experience. I liked that. I --

So you started doing this in the mid-50's, I guess, with Capitol --
I remember we used to get a lot of Frank Sinatra stuff that used to come in there from somewhere.
You weren't playing so much then?
No. I was doing more writing.
And when I got into my own thing like in '59, you know,when we started doing these rock and roll records -- you know, rhythm and blues records, I wasn't doing any playing.
I just wasn't playing and just publishing (inaudible) --
